title: Design a Distributed Key-Value Store (DynamoDB)
subtitle: Consistent hashing, vector clocks, quorum reads/writes (R + W > N), and LSM trees

stages.title: Stage 1 — Single-Node LSM Tree Key-Value Engine
stages.bottleneck: Memory limits on single server; random write disk I/O bottleneck.

edges.label: Flush MemTable to disk when full

stages.narrative: **LSM Tree Architecture.** High write throughput engine. All writes are appended sequentially to a WAL and stored in an in-memory MemTable (SkipList). When MemTable fills, it flushes to immutable SSTables on disk.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Hash Ring Partitioning & Quorum Consensus (N, R, W)
stages.bottleneck: Network partitions across nodes (CAP theorem tradeoff).
stages.narrative:
**Quorum Reads & Writes (`R + W > N`).**
With replication factor `N = 3`, write quorum `W = 2`, read quorum `R = 2`.

Since `R + W = 4 > 3`, at least one node in the read quorum is guaranteed to contain the latest write.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Anti-Entropy Merkle Trees & Vector Clock Conflict Resolution
stages.bottleneck: Concurrent conflicting updates from different regions.
stages.narrative:
**Anti-Entropy with Merkle Trees & Vector Clocks.**
1. **Merkle Trees:** Nodes quickly compare hierarchical hash trees to discover data divergence without comparing raw key ranges.
2. **Vector Clocks:** Detect causal relationship and concurrent conflicts (`D1([A:1])` vs `D2([A:1, B:1])`).
